Monitoring with Grafana & Graphite

Understand enterprise monitoring with grafana, graphite and statsD

Monitoring and observability is extremely crucial for the success of any software solution meant for high scale. Importance of these parameters become more visible when the load increase over the period of time.

In the world of microservices and distributed monoliths, monitoring metrics of hundreds of services becomes a challenge if you are not fully equipped. Since its a common hurdle, multiple solutions are readily available in the market. One of the beloved open source solution is Grafana coupled with Graphite and StatsD.

Don’t worry, I will explain those terms which sounds jargon to you.

What is StatsD ?

StatsD is an open source network daemon which ingests data into one or more pluggable backend services. Consider it like a transporter for the metrics data to one or more services. It build with infamous Node.js.

StatsD runs on default port 8125. It supports both transports UDP and TCP. StatsD supports 4 metric types:

  1. Counters (c)
  2. Timers (ms)
  3. Gauge (g)
  4. Sets (s)

Read more about them on statsd metric types. You can send metrics to StatsD in the following format

<metricname>:<value>|<type>

Run StatsD using docker

docker run -d -n statsd -p 8125:8125/udp statsd/statsd

Send counter metrics to the statsD listening on port 8125

echo "myapplication.service.metric:20|c" | nc -w 1 -u <ip-address> 8125

What is Graphite ?

Graphite is an open source time series aggregation and storage tool. Well! you must be wondering why do we need it. StatsD is not a storage solution and it requires some pluggable service to ingest the data. Graphite is that pluggable service which will receive data from StatsD and can also aggregate it as per the need.

Graphite comprise of 3 components

  1. Carbon
  2. Whisper
  3. Graphite web

Carbon

Carbon is an ingestion layer which receives the data from monitoring tool and buffers it before storing to a time series database called Whisper which we will discuss later. It decouples data ingestion from storage itself which is crucial for scalability. It can be configured using /etc/carbon/carbon.conf

It comprise of 3 components

  • Carbon Cache
    It is the central daemon (single threaded) responsible for writing incoming metrics to storage (usually Whisper). It acts as an in-memory cache to reduce disk I/O, aggregating data points before persisting them. You can spin multiple carbon-cache instances to handle load.
    Can be configured using /etc/carbon/storage-schemas.conf and /etc/carbon/storage-aggregation.conf
  • Carbon Relay
    It is a lightweight daemon that routes incoming metrics to appropriate Carbon Cache instances or other relays. It supports sharding, load balancing, and replication, ensuring efficient data distribution in high-throughput environments. It more or less a reverse proxy for caches.
    Can be configured using /etc/carbon/relay-rules.conf
  • Carbon Aggregator (optional)
    It preprocesses metrics by combining multiple data points into summarized ones before forwarding them to a Carbon Cache or Relay. Dont think its optional, hence not important. Aggregator rules actually define how metrics should be aggregated, ensuring that only relevant, condensed data is stored, which is critical for long-term retention.
    Can be configured using /etc/carbon/aggregation-rules.conf

Whisper

Whisper is an optimsed file based time series database which stores the metrics in format of multiple .wsp files depending on the configuration provided in /etc/carbon/storage-schemas.conf and /etc/carbon/storage-aggregation.conf

Graphite Web

Its the Graphical User Interface for visualising graphs and dashboard but I don’t think the focus was visualisation at that time as UI is terrible. It is more oriented towards faster and efficient retrieval of data from storage system. Lack of visualisation takes us to the Grafana which we will discuss next.

Runs Graphite and StatsD using docker

docker run -d -n graphite-statsd
 -p 80:80\
 -p 2003-2004:2003-2004\
 -p 2023-2024:2023-2024\
 -p 8125:8125/udp\
 -p 8126:8126\
 graphiteapp/graphite-statsd

Grafana

Modern age visualisation tool which is fully customisable and allows integration with various data sources like Kubernetes clusters, postgresDB, influxDB, MSSQL, ElasticSearch, Graphite, AWS Cloudwatch. Grafana is required because visualisation provided by graphite web is very rudimentary and in my opinion ‘terrible’. Grafana is an industry standard tool at the time of this article. It also provides alerting out of the box.

Image how much of information you can receive about you system. Trust me it will save you hell lot of time and effort and sometimes spare you from doing ssh into multiple nodes protected by crazy firewalls just to get the logs.

Grafana runs on default port 3000.

Run Grafana using docker

docker run -d --name=grafana -p 3000:3000 grafana/grafana

Conclusion

Grafana can be coupled with Graphite or even better alternative such as prometheus and influxDB (superior in my opinion) to establish monitoring, observability and alerting in a distributed system. As monitoring is as important as architectural design on an enterprise scale for the success of team and product.

“ Monitoring is like the nervous system of your infrastructure, ensuring everything runs smoothly and responds to stress signals before they escalate. “
